alt.en: A printed book page in old type: a short rule, the heading "After Harvest" in black-letter, "HYMN CXVI", the first verse beginning "Come, ye thankful people, come, Raise the song of Harvest-home!" and six lines of the second verse beginning "We ourselves are God's own field", with the signature mark "o 2" at the foot.
alt.es: Página de un libro impreso en tipografía antigua: una raya corta, el encabezamiento "After Harvest" en letra gótica, "HYMN CXVI", la primera estrofa, que empieza "Come, ye thankful people, come, Raise the song of Harvest-home!", y seis versos de la segunda, que empieza "We ourselves are God's own field", con la marca de pliego "o 2" al pie.

caption.en: Hymn CXVI, "After Harvest", on page 147 of Alford's Psalms and Hymns (London, 1844), the book he made for his parish of Wymeswold and the hymn's earliest printing, with his first line for verse 2, "We ourselves are God's own field".
caption.es: El himno CXVI, "After Harvest", en la página 147 de Psalms and Hymns de Alford (Londres, 1844), el himnario que preparó para su parroquia de Wymeswold y la primera impresión del himno, con su primer verso original de la estrofa 2, "We ourselves are God's own field".

source: Henry Alford, Psalms and Hymns, adapted to the Sundays and Holydays throughout the Year (London, 1844), p. 147, Hymn CXVI, "After Harvest"
library: Oxford University (digitized by Google, hosted by the Internet Archive)

alt.en: A printed music page headed "Harvest." in black-letter and "Hymn 223.", with four systems of a hymn tune in four parts on two staves, with one sharp in the key signature and no words.
alt.es: Página de música impresa con el encabezamiento "Harvest." en letra gótica y "Hymn 223.", con cuatro sistemas de una melodía de himno a cuatro voces en dos pentagramas, con un sostenido en la armadura y sin letra.

caption.en: Hymn 223 under "Harvest" in the first music edition of Hymns Ancient and Modern (London, 1861): George Elvey's tune in four parts, the harmony our arrangement is built on, with the compilers' rewritten words on the facing page.
caption.es: El himno 223, en la sección "Harvest", en la primera edición con música de Hymns Ancient and Modern (Londres, 1861): la melodía de George Elvey a cuatro voces, la armonía en la que se basa nuestro arreglo, con la letra reescrita por los compiladores en la página de enfrente.

source: Hymns Ancient and Modern for Use in the Services of the Church, with Accompanying Tunes, ed. William Henry Monk (London: Novello, 1861), Hymn 223, "Harvest"
library: University of Toronto, Faculty of Music Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: M2136 .H97 1861 MUSI; Internet Archive hymnsancientmode00unse, image n311
licenceEvidence: Published London 1861; Elvey died 1893, Monk 1889, Alford 1871. Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
credit: University of Toronto, Faculty of Music Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: An early sepia photograph on a grey mount: the side of a tall Gothic chapel with large pointed traceried windows, buttresses topped by pinnacles and a battlemented parapet, a low porch with a pointed doorway at the left, a castle wall at the right, and a sloping empty roadway in front.
alt.es: Fotografía antigua en sepia sobre un soporte gris: el costado de una alta capilla gótica con grandes ventanales apuntados con tracería, contrafuertes rematados por pináculos y un parapeto almenado, un pórtico bajo con una puerta apuntada a la izquierda, un muro del castillo a la derecha y, delante, un camino vacío en cuesta.

caption.en: St George's Chapel, Windsor, photographed by William Henry Fox Talbot about 1843 to 1847: George Elvey was its organist from 1835 to 1882, and his tune for this hymn is named after it.
caption.es: La capilla de San Jorge de Windsor, fotografiada por William Henry Fox Talbot hacia 1843 a 1847: George Elvey fue su organista de 1835 a 1882, y su melodía para este himno lleva su nombre.

source: William Henry Fox Talbot, St. George's Chapel, Windsor, salted paper print, c. 1843/47
